title: California LifeLine
resource-description: Discounted phone or broadband service for one eligible household based on income or participation in programs such as Medi-Cal, CalFresh, SSI, WIC, CalWORKs, or federal housing assistance.
contact: Start enrollment through a participating phone or internet provider or call 877-858-7463

title: Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants
resource-description: Monthly California cash benefits for eligible aged, blind, or disabled non-citizens who cannot receive SSI solely because of immigration status and meet income and resource limits.
contact: Apply through the county social services office where you live

title: Beyond Emancipation Educational Support
resource-description: Transcript review, high-school diploma and GED referrals, college enrollment, financial-aid and application help, study-skills coaching, textbook assistance, and scholarship support for eligible Alameda-connected foster or probation youth.
contact: Call 510-667-7696 to get started

title: Beyond Emancipation Transition Support
resource-description: Coaching and practical support before and after emancipation for current and former foster or probation youth, focused on achievable goals and a stable transition to adulthood.
contact: Call 510-980-9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org

title: Alameda County Youth Transitions Partnership
resource-description: Intensive coaching and DBT skills groups for Alameda County foster youth, non-minor dependents, and former foster youth ages 14 to 24, supporting education, employment, housing stability, and permanent connections.
contact: Call First Place Alameda at 510-272-0979 and ask about Youth Transitions Partnership

title: Fred Finch Transitions
resource-description: Community-based individual, family, and group therapy, rehabilitation, clinical case management, and medication support for eligible Alameda County youth ages 15.5 to 25 with moderate to severe mental-health needs and full-scope Medi-Cal.
contact: Call the program director at 510-846-9966 for referral information

title: Fred Finch STAY
resource-description: Community-based mental-health, medication, housing-stability, education, and supported-employment services for eligible young adults ages 18 to 24 in North and Central Alameda County with serious mental-health and housing challenges.
contact: Start through Alameda County ACCESS at 800-491-9099 or call 510-846-9966

title: Fred Finch Therapeutic Behavioral Services
resource-description: Intensive one-to-one behavioral coaching at home or in the community for Alameda County youth under 21 with serious emotional challenges and full-scope Medi-Cal.
contact: Call 650-537-2328 or email jenniferjimenez@fredfinch.org

title: Fred Finch Visiting Therapist Program
resource-description: Trauma-informed therapy, case support, and caregiver peer support for Alameda County youth ages 3 to 21 involved with child welfare or juvenile justice who have active Alameda County Medi-Cal.
contact: Call 510-773-7345 or email VTPintake@fredfinch.org

title: Fred Finch Alameda In-Home Services
resource-description: Individual and family counseling, case management, and 24/7 crisis-call availability for eligible Alameda County youth ages 3 to 21 with active Medi-Cal who are at risk of losing a home or foster placement.
contact: Use the referral and contact information on the program page

title: Fred Finch Enhanced Care Management
resource-description: No-cost intensive care coordination for eligible children and young adults in a managed-care Medi-Cal plan, including people through age 26 with a history of foster care.
contact: Use the referral and contact information on the program page

title: Alameda County Permanent Youth Connections
resource-description: Family-finding and permanency support for children, foster youth, and non-minor dependents receiving placement or transition-to-adulthood services, including connections to relatives and other caring adults.
contact: Ask your Alameda County child welfare worker about a Permanent Youth Connections referral

title: Covenant House Oakland TAY Housing Resource Center
resource-description: Youth-focused coordinated-entry access point and housing problem-solving service for Alameda County young adults ages 18 to 24 experiencing homelessness.
contact: Call 510-379-1010 or visit 200 Harrison Street Oakland during posted drop-in hours

title: My First Place Contra Costa County
resource-description: Shared-apartment housing plus education, employment, case-management, and housing support for young adults ages 18 to 25 who have experienced foster care in Contra Costa County.
contact: Call 925-771-3100 or email info@firstplaceforyouth.org

title: Rainbow Community Center Youth Group
resource-description: Weekly affirming peer group, leadership development, activities, and resource connections for LGBTQIA2S+ youth ages 12 to 25 in Contra Costa County.
contact: Email Bianca@rainbowcc.org or call 925-692-0090

title: Rainbow Community Center Clinical Services
resource-description: Affirming trauma-informed individual, family, and adolescent therapy plus sexual-health services for LGBTQIA2S+ people, including youth and young adults.
contact: Request an appointment online or call 925-692-0090

title: Community Violence Solutions Crisis Support
resource-description: Free confidential 24/7 crisis response, safety planning, counseling, accompaniment, advocacy, and case management for sexual-assault and human-trafficking survivors in Contra Costa County.
contact: Call 800-670-7273 or text CVS to 20121

title: Youth Homes Family Pathways
resource-description: Intensive care coordination, home-based services, and individual or family therapy for Contra Costa County youth ages 0 to 21 referred by Behavioral Health, including foster youth and youth at risk of entering care.
contact: Ask Contra Costa Behavioral Health Services about a Family Pathways referral

title: Contra Costa Youth Service Bureau Wraparound
resource-description: Team-based mental-health, life-coaching, family-advocacy, crisis-prevention, education, and vocational support for Medi-Cal-eligible youth ages 5 to 21 and their families.
contact: Call 510-215-4670 or use the Wraparound referral form

title: Contra Costa Youth Service Bureau Kinship Program
resource-description: Case management, advocacy, support groups, peer mentoring, respite, transportation, tutoring, independent-living skills, and youth development for relative caregivers and children in West Contra Costa County.
contact: Call 510-215-4670 or download the Kinship application

title: Contra Costa Youth Service Bureau Therapy Services
resource-description: Trauma-informed individual, family, and group therapy for Contra Costa County youth ages 5 to 21 and their caregivers experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, family conflict, or school difficulties.
contact: Call 510-215-4670 or email info@wccysb.org

title: Contra Costa Youth Service Bureau Workforce Development
resource-description: Career coaching, job-readiness training, paid internships, placement help, financial literacy, GED support, and college or trade-school navigation for youth ages 16 to 24 facing employment or education barriers.
contact: Call 510-215-4670 or email info@wccysb.org

title: Contra Costa Family Justice Center TeleCare
resource-description: Free virtual medical appointments and wraparound connections regardless of insurance for Contra Costa County survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse, elder abuse, or human trafficking.
contact: Contact or visit a Contra Costa Family Justice Center and ask about TeleCare

title: Antioch SOAR Youth Apprenticeship
resource-description: Periodic youth-apprenticeship cohorts with one-to-one mentoring, job-readiness training, professional development, and transportation support for eligible Antioch youth.
contact: Check the City of Antioch page for the next cohort application window

title: Contra Costa Youth Partner Program
resource-description: Peer-to-peer mentorship, guidance, rights education, and advocacy from young adults with lived foster-care experience for youth ages 10 to 21 involved with Contra Costa Children and Family Services.
contact: Contact the Child Abuse Prevention Council at 925-798-0546 and ask for Youth Partners

title: Child Advocates of Contra Costa Tutor Program
resource-description: Weekly one-to-one educational support from trauma-informed volunteer tutors for K-12 children and youth in foster care or the juvenile-justice system.
contact: Ask a social worker or Child Advocates at 925-256-7284 about student matching

title: Crossroads High School for Parenting Students
resource-description: Alternative high-school instruction, parenting support, and free on-site Head Start childcare for enrolled pregnant or parenting students in the Mt. Diablo Unified School District.
contact: Call Crossroads High School at 925-689-6852
